steps.title: Run SEC and collect fractions
steps.instruction: Load the serum‑converted platelet lysate (SCPL) onto a commercial size‑exclusion chromatography (SEC) column (or an agarose/Sephadex column) and elute with DPBS, collecting 20 sequential fractions (≈1 mL each). Fractions 1‑4 are DPBS flow‑through, fractions 5‑12 contain low protein, fractions 13‑16 contain the bulk of free proteins, and fractions 7‑11 are enriched in EVs (80‑120 nm).

substeps.instruction: Prepare the SEC column according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Apply the SCPL sample to the column.
Elute with DPBS at the recommended flow rate.

steps.title: Measure protein concentration
steps.instruction: Determine protein concentration in each fraction using a protein assay (BCA, Bradford) or spectrophotometry at 280 nm (e.g., Nanodrop). Expect low/undetectable protein in fractions 1‑4, a rise after fraction 10, and a peak between fractions 13‑16.

steps.title: Assess particle size and count
steps.instruction: Analyze particle size distribution of each fraction (or selected fractions) using nanoparticle tracking analysis (NTA) or dynamic light scattering (DLS). NTA also provides particle concentration. Fractions 7‑11 should show a high concentration of 80‑120 nm vesicles; later fractions (>10) show particles <20 nm.

steps.title: Optional cryo‑EM imaging
steps.instruction: Perform cryo‑electron microscopy on selected fractions to visually confirm the presence of lipid‑bilayer vesicles (EVs) versus protein aggregates.

steps.title: Quantify non‑EV proteins by ELISA
steps.instruction: Use ELISA kits to measure concentrations of common non‑EV components such as apolipoproteins, albumin, and immunoglobulins in both EV‑enriched and protein‑rich fractions.

steps.title: Validate EV marker proteins
steps.instruction: Measure canonical EV markers (CD9, CD81, ALIX, TSG101, syntenin‑1) in the pooled EV fractions (e.g., fractions 7‑11) by western blot, flow cytometry, or ELISA.

steps.title: Assess platelet‑specific markers
steps.instruction: Detect platelet membrane proteins CD41 (GPIIb), CD42b (GPIb), CD61 (GPIIIa), and CD62P (P‑selectin) in the EV fractions to confirm platelet origin.

steps.title: Calculate particle‑to‑protein ratio
steps.instruction: Divide particle count (from NTA) by protein concentration (from assay) for each EV‑containing fraction and report the ratio as a purity metric.

steps.title: Optional proteomic profiling
steps.instruction: Perform mass‑spectrometry‑based proteomics on selected fractions to identify the most abundant proteins.

steps.title: Isolate and quantify EV miRNA
steps.instruction: Extract miRNA from EV fractions using the qEV miRNA isolation kit (Izon, catalog RXT01). Quantify miRNA with the Qiagen LNA‑based qPCR system, including synthetic spike‑in miRNAs to control for isolation, reverse transcription, and amplification efficiency.

steps.title: Functional assays on cultured cells
steps.instruction: Test biological activity of platelet lysate or isolated EVs on target cells. Use a starting concentration of 1 % v/v platelet lysate for screening; for isolated EVs dose based on protein concentration or particle count. Include a blank containing culture medium plus EVs without cells to subtract background in viability (MTT, WST, CCK‑8) or injury (LDH) assays.

steps.title: Concentrate dilute EV fractions
steps.instruction: If SEC fractions are too dilute, concentrate EVs using centrifugal filter columns with an appropriate molecular‑weight cutoff, or by ultracentrifugation to pellet EVs (note that some loss may occur).
